From parts counted against the ideal cycle time. Each operation in the Parts List carries an ideal cycle time and a quantity per cycle, and the parts gauge divides the parts made by what that cycle time allows in the machine’s running time. A press running all shift at 40 strokes a minute against an ideal of 60 shows a green uptime gauge and a red parts gauge.
Datwyler molds precision components on more than 20 injection molding machines in California. Every stop now carries a reason, and the weekly and monthly reports show which ones to fix next.

A downtime category: a reason created under a severity heading, optionally requiring a note, optionally marked as planned downtime, tagged with a type and given a color that carries through to the Downtimes report. Keep the list to about eight reasons, so operators pick from it without scrolling.

Planned downtime is a stop you scheduled: a changeover, a preventive maintenance window, a break. In IoTFlows it is a setting on the reason, so every stop classified under Tool Change is planned and every stop under Machine Failure is not. Planned reasons carry a calendar icon in the picker, which filters to planned or unplanned reasons in one click.

Yes. The Classify Downtime dialog carries a Create Maintenance Workorder button, so a stop caused by a fault becomes a work order in Maintain with the reason as its title, the note as its description and the machine already set. An event rule or a meter can open one too.

One. A sensor is attached to exactly one asset, the record that represents one machine, and one sensor per machine is the unit IoTFlows counts, bills and reports on. A multi-spindle machine sometimes carries more than one.
